correctness.rationale: Translation and dual restriction reduce the problem to the span of support differences with multiplicity \(2^{d-r}\). For affine rank two the support is the whole four-point plane; invertibility of the Walsh matrix plus avoidance of finitely many proper hyperplanes realizes every nonempty local Fourier support. For affine rank three, two adjacent zeros force one slope coefficient to vanish, two antipodal zeros force the constant coefficient to vanish, so every zero pair has Hamming distance two. Four mutually distance-two cube vertices form a parity tetrahedron whose four equations sum to \(4a=0\), impossible over \(\mathbb C\) with nonzero constant coefficient. Explicit witnesses realize zero counts zero through three. An independent rational nullspace replay in this audit found exactly 1 empty, 8 singleton, 12 distance-two pair, and 8 three-point feasible zero patterns.
correctness.risk: The result assumes complex coefficients with exact four-point support; coefficient-orbit geometry is not classified.

value.rationale: Four-sparse uncertainty is the first support size at which affine planes and affine-independent bases diverge in binary vector spaces. The theorem gives a complete all-dimensional spectrum and explains every local zero geometry, a natural structural classification rather than a finite table.

final_claim: For every \(d\ge3\), exact four-point supports in \(\mathbb F_2^d\) have only two affine types. Affine planes attain local Fourier-support sizes \(1,2,3,4\), affine-independent supports attain \(5,6,7,8\), and therefore the global exact-support-four spectrum is \(\{2,4,5,6,7,8\}2^{d-3}\); in the independent case the exact zero patterns are the empty set, singletons, distance-two pairs, and three vertices of a parity tetrahedron.
limitations: Exact four-point support on elementary Abelian two-groups only.
No classification of coefficient orbits beyond Fourier zero patterns.
